The '''Iron Citadel''' was a mythical massive [[stone]] [[palace]] on the [[Deep Core]] [[planet]] [[Empress Teta]]. According to the quasi-historical [[Qel-Droma Epics]], it was once home to the crown of Koros Major and was eventually conquered by the [[Krath]]. At some point, it served as the headquarters of the fallen [[Jedi]] [[Ulic Qel-Droma]]. By the time of the [[Imperial Era]], many outside the [[Empress Teta system]] doubted that it ever existed at all.

{{Struct-stub}}

==History==
According to the quasi-historical [[Qel-Droma Epics]], the Iron Citadel was named for its iron battlements and was thought impenetrable. Having repelled invasion and infiltration by the [[Galactic Republic]], [[Mandalorian]]s, [[Sith]] and the [[Jedi Order]], the Iron Citadel was eventually conquered by the [[Krath]] following a [[Conquest of the Empress Teta system|military coup]] and served as a command center in their bloody [[Crusade of Krath|crusade]] against the Jedi Order. The epics further stated that [[Mandalorian crusaders|Mandalorian Crusaders]] serving under Qel-Droma rode [[Basilisk war droid]]s into combat out of the fortress.<ref name="NOP" />

Despite being regarded as a legendary site, Qel-Droma Epics scholars during the Imperial era made fruitless expeditions trying to find the ancient battlegrounds and relics from a lost age of heroes. Among the rumored artifacts to be housed within the ruins were the [[Ulic Qel-Droma's Lightsaber Crystal|lightsaber crystal]] of Ulic-Qel Droma, the Krath [[Translation Talisman]] of [[Satal Keto]], and an operational Basilisk war droid. Many outside the [[Empress Teta system]] doubted that it ever existed at all. Locals on the planet insisted that it formed the foundations of the modern [[Tetan Royal Palace]], while a small minority believed that it was buried deep beneath the [[Royal District|modern cityscape]] and served as a shrine for surviving Krath loyalists. Others believed the Republic destroyed the citadel while retaking the system from the Krath.<ref name="NOP" />
